p1_b9.ocr: isolates sampled from the same area/region showed var- iation for NaCl tolerance (compare Figure 3 and Table 2). 55.41% of the isolates (which includes 14 isolates of S. medicae) had good tolerance to NaCl (> 513 mM), indicating that the rhizobia nodulating alfalfa are more tolerant compared to other rhizobia species [3,18]. Four S. meliloti isolates (# 44, 45, 142 and 143) had greater tolerance to salt (1711 mM NaCl), which were sampled

p1_b10.ocr: from the highly salt-affected areas of southern Morocco, than others, indicating that saline soils naturally select strains more tolerant to salinity, and results in higher recovery of salinity-tolerant strains. The isolates recovered displayed tolerance response to water stress, 82.16% of the isolates grew at water stress of -1.5 MPa (Figure 2b).
